intervention_label: ACBI4 (VHL-recruiting PROTAC degrader of GTP-loaded KRAS)
mechanism: ACBI4 is a heterobifunctional molecule that bridges the VHL E3 ligase to KRAS in its GTP-loaded state, forming a cooperative ternary complex that routes the protein to the proteasome. Because the handle is the active conformation rather than a mutant-specific cysteine or aspartate, alleles with no covalent chemistry of their own, G12R among them, become addressable. Degradation removes the scaffolding functions of KRAS as well as its catalytic output, which inhibitor occupancy does not.
rationale: G12R has no selective inhibitor and the covalent arginine chemistry has not moved past a crystal structure in four years, so a modality that does not need allele-specific chemistry is worth watching for this patient. The Dundee group reported potent degradation of KRAS G12R specifically, with antiproliferative effect in KRAS-driven cells. It is orthogonal to daraxonrasib: one occupies RAS(ON), the other removes it, and the reported daraxonrasib escape route in G12R cells (leaning on EGFR-driven wild-type RAS-GTP) would also be degraded here.
novelty: A published chemical tool from an academic degrader group with no IND, no company program, and no registered trial in any indication; the pan-RAS agents upstream are occupancy inhibitors, not degraders.

key_manuscripts.finding: Screening VHL-based PROTACs against GTP-loaded KRAS produced ACBI4, which forms a highly cooperative ternary complex and potently degrades KRAS G12R with an antiproliferative effect in KRAS-mutant cells. The authors position it as a chemical tool for degrading KRAS(ON) alleles that current pan-KRAS inhibitors and degraders cannot reach.

developability: A tool compound, not a drug: bifunctional VHL degraders of this size carry the usual permeability and oral-exposure problems, and nothing has been dosed in an animal tumor model yet. Getting to a patient would need a degrader with drug-like properties, PDAC in-vivo work, and an IND.
risks: No in-vivo efficacy or tolerability data; potency in cells does not predict exposure in tissue
Degrading GTP-loaded KRAS also hits wild-type RAS-GTP in normal cells, and the therapeutic index is unmeasured
No PDAC model in the paper, so the G12R activity is shown in cell lines of other lineages
VHL-based degraders are vulnerable to ligase downregulation as a resistance route
caveats: The reported G12R activity comes from one paper and has not been reproduced by an independent group.

intervention_label: PI3Kgamma blockade of KRAS-independent macropinocytosis (eganelisib / IPI-549 as the available tool)
mechanism: G12R cannot engage p110alpha because switch II is distorted, so it does not drive macropinocytosis the way G12D and G12V do. Hobbs and colleagues found that G12R PDAC lines instead run macropinocytic nutrient scavenging through KRAS-independent PI3Kgamma and RAC1. Blocking p110gamma would cut a supply line that in this allele sits outside the KRAS node itself, which is also why a RAS inhibitor would not close it.
rationale: The nutrient-scavenging dependency in G12R sits downstream of a different lipid kinase than in G12D, and eganelisib is a p110gamma-selective molecule that already has human pharmacology from myeloid-directed immuno-oncology work. Nobody has taken it into a macropinocytosis-blocking, allele-directed indication. As a partner for a pan-RAS agent in a G12R tumor it is at least mechanistically coherent, since it would starve the cell of the scavenged protein that buffers RAS-pathway suppression.
novelty: No oncology program pairs a PI3Kgamma inhibitor with the G12R macropinocytosis dependency; the clinical eganelisib work was myeloid reprogramming, an unrelated rationale, and nothing on this mechanism appears upstream.

key_manuscripts.finding: G12R was defective for p110alpha binding and failed to drive macropinocytosis, but KRAS-independent PI3Kgamma activity sustained it, and 300 nM IPI-549 lowered macropinocytosis in every G12R line tested. No growth, survival, or in-vivo readout was reported for PI3Kgamma inhibition.

developability: Eganelisib has been through human dosing, so a window or combination study is conceivable, but the preclinical case is a single uptake assay with no anti-tumor endpoint. Somebody would have to show that blocking macropinocytosis actually slows a G12R PDAC model before this is worth a protocol.
risks: IPI-549 also reduced macropinocytosis in G12D and G12V lines, so the effect is not G12R-selective and the allele rationale may be weaker than it looks
No evidence that blocking scavenging translates into growth inhibition, let alone regression
PI3Kgamma inhibition reshapes myeloid cells, which could cut either way in a T-cell-poor PDAC microenvironment
Nutrient scavenging has redundant routes (autophagy, entosis) that would likely compensate
caveats: One paper, one assay endpoint, no replication and no animal data.

intervention_label: CDK8/19 inhibition added to RAS(ON) inhibition (with or without CTLA-4 blockade)
mechanism: Blocking mutant KRAS in PDAC opens a short immune window: dendritic cells and T cells move in next to cancer cells. CDK8, a mediator-complex kinase, closes it again by driving CXCL2 secretion and holding FAS expression down, and the microenvironment reverts to an immune-evasive state that carries the tumor into resistance. Inhibiting CDK8 during RAS suppression keeps the window open rather than trying to reopen it later.
rationale: This patient's tumor is MSS with TMB 0.83, so the only plausible immune route is one that is manufactured by another drug rather than pre-existing, and RAS inhibition is the manufacturer. The same CDK8 upregulation was seen in PDX tumors that had become resistant to daraxonrasib and to zoldonrasib, which is the class most likely to be used here. Kalluri's group showed CDK8 targeting alone or with anti-CTLA-4 reversed resistance to KRAS G12D inhibition in vivo.
novelty: No registered trial pairs a CDK8/19 inhibitor with a RAS(ON) inhibitor in any tumor type; the upstream file carries the CDK8 finding as a resistance mechanism, not as an intervention.

key_manuscripts.finding: Long-term MRTX1133 treatment reversed the early immune influx through CDK8-driven CXCL2 induction and FAS suppression, and targeting CDK8 alone or with anti-CTLA-4 overcame resistance. CDK8 was also upregulated in PDX tumors resistant to daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib.

model_systems: KRAS G12D GEMM and orthotopic PDAC models
developability: CDK8/19 inhibitors exist as clinical-grade molecules in other indications, so the missing piece is a combination protocol and a tolerability read on adding a mediator-kinase inhibitor to a pan-RAS backbone, not new chemistry.
risks: The in-vivo work used a G12D-selective tool compound; whether the same CDK8 program governs escape in a G12R tumor is untested, and G12R adapts through EGFR-driven wild-type RAS rather than mutant KRAS
CDK8 loss has tumor-suppressive as well as tumor-promoting effects depending on context, so the direction of effect is not guaranteed
Adding CTLA-4 blockade brings real toxicity for a benefit shown only in mice
Overlapping myelosuppression and GI toxicity with a RAS backbone is unquantified
caveats: Single laboratory, single publication; no independent replication of the CDK8 resistance axis yet.

intervention_label: KRAS G12R-directed TCR discovery and ex-vivo priming (allele extension of an existing platform)
mechanism: Mutant KRAS peptides are shared, public neoantigens, and TCR-T against G12D and G12V works by redirecting T cells to those peptides on the patient's HLA. A published ex-vivo priming process starts from healthy-donor blood, primes against a chosen KRAS neoepitope on the donor's HLA background, and clones the resulting receptors. Applying it to the G12R peptide would produce the reagent that does not currently exist.
rationale: Every mutant-KRAS cell therapy this patient could be offered is restricted to G12D or G12V; the coverage gap for G12R is documented upstream as an eligibility exclusion, not as a biological one. In a tumor that is MSS with almost no mutational burden, a shared driver neoantigen is one of the few antigens that is certainly there. The platform is agnostic to which hotspot it is run against, and its authors name G12R explicitly as the untried extension.
novelty: No G12R-reactive TCR has been published, no G12R cell-therapy trial exists, and this is a discovery step rather than a molecule, so nothing upstream can be covering it.

key_manuscripts.finding: A single ex-vivo process primed and expanded T cells against 46 of 47 evaluated KRAS neoantigens across 20 healthy donors and yielded more than 150 cloned TCRs, some matching clinically active benchmarks in potency. The authors focused on G12D and G12V and state that G12R is a target the process could be applied to but was not.

model_systems: in-vitro and in-vivo tumor-growth assays with engineered T cells
developability: Nothing exists to give a patient. The path runs through epitope confirmation on the relevant HLA alleles, receptor isolation, affinity and cross-reactivity screening, then a manufacturing and IND package, which is several years even if the biology cooperates.
risks: The G12R peptide may simply not be presented well on this patient's HLA type; that is an empirical question nobody has answered
HLA typing for this case is not in the record, so eligibility for any such product is unknown
Off-target and alloreactivity screening for a new receptor is a real safety burden, as fatal cross-reactivity has occurred with other engineered TCRs
PDAC stromal exclusion has blunted every adoptive-cell approach tried so far, whatever the antigen
caveats: This is a research direction with no compound and no timeline attached; it belongs in the horizon scan, not in any near-term plan.

intervention_label: p53 Y220C reactivation paired with a BH3 mimetic to raise apoptotic priming
mechanism: Whether restored p53 kills a cell or only stops it dividing is set upstream of p53, by how close the mitochondria already sit to the apoptotic threshold. KRAS-driven epithelial tumors sit far from it, holding reserve BCL-2 and BCL-XL capacity, and they arrest. A BH3 mimetic occupies that reserve, so the transcriptional output of restored p53 lands on a primed mitochondrion and the same signal produces apoptosis instead.
rationale: This case pairs a Y220C reactivator route with a KRAS driver, which is exactly the configuration Sanchez-Rivera modelled: p53 restoration in Kras-mutant epithelial tumors gave arrest, and navitoclax or BCL-2/BCL-XL deletion converted it to apoptosis in vitro and in vivo. If rezatapopt-class agents underperform in KRAS-mutant solid tumors, low priming is a specific, testable reason rather than a generic one. The combination has not been built, and BH3 profiling of a patient's tumor could say in advance whether it is worth building.
novelty: No trial or program combines a p53 Y220C reactivator with a BH3 mimetic; the upstream file carries the priming paper as background mechanism for rezatapopt rather than as a combination candidate.

key_manuscripts.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
key_manuscripts.finding: In p53-restorable Kras-driven lung adenocarcinoma and sarcoma lines, low mitochondrial priming produced cell-cycle arrest rather than death, and priming the cells genetically or with navitoclax turned p53 restoration into apoptosis in vitro and in vivo.

model_systems: Kras-driven p53-restorable GEMM lines (lung adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, lymphoma)
developability: Both halves exist as clinical-grade molecules, so this is a combination-design problem rather than a discovery one. What is missing is the experiment: a Y220C reactivator plus a BH3 mimetic in a KRAS-mutant, Y220C PDAC model, with BH3 profiling as the selection assay.
risks: Navitoclax brings dose-limiting thrombocytopenia through BCL-XL, which is the arm doing the work here; a BCL-XL degrader would be the way around it but adds its own unknowns
The supporting model restored wild-type p53 genetically, which is a cleaner and probably stronger signal than a small molecule refolding Y220C
No PDAC model and no Y220C model in the supporting work
Overlapping marrow toxicity with anything cytotoxic this patient might also need
caveats: Cross-tumor and cross-mechanism inference: the p53 restoration was genetic, in mouse lung and sarcoma tumors, not pharmacologic Y220C rescue in PDAC.

intervention_label: Statin-driven degradation of misfolded p53 via the mevalonate-DNAJA1 axis
mechanism: Y220C destabilises the DNA-binding domain, and the misfolded protein survives because DNAJA1, an Hsp40 chaperone, holds it away from CHIP-mediated ubiquitylation. Statins cut mevalonate-5-phosphate, which weakens the DNAJA1 interaction and releases the mutant protein for nuclear export and proteasomal degradation. The approach removes the mutant protein rather than trying to refold it.
rationale: Iwakuma's screen found that statins deplete conformational mutants specifically, and the Y220C example they used was BxPC-3, a pancreatic line, which is unusually close to this case for a chemical-biology paper. Statins are cheap, familiar, and already taken by many patients in this age band. The argument for looking at them here is that they attack the same lesion as a reactivator from the opposite direction, so they stay relevant if the reactivator route closes.
novelty: No oncology development program or trial selects patients by conformational TP53 mutation for statin therapy; the upstream files carry only reactivator chemistry for this feature.

key_manuscripts.finding: A high-throughput screen identified statins as degradation inducers for conformational p53 mutants, with lovastatin depleting p53 Y220C in the pancreatic line BxPC-3, while sparing wild-type p53 and DNA-contact mutants such as R273H. Degradation ran through loss of mevalonate-5-phosphate, weakened DNAJA1 binding, and CHIP-mediated ubiquitylation.

model_systems: conformational vs contact mutant cell panel
developability: Off-patent and orally available, so an investigator-initiated window or biomarker-selected study is feasible without new chemistry. The open question is whether achievable plasma statin levels reproduce the mutant-p53 depletion seen at in-vitro concentrations, which is the usual failure point for statin repurposing.
risks: Directly antagonistic to a Y220C reactivator: degrading the protein removes the substrate rezatapopt-class drugs are meant to refold, so the two cannot be given together
In-vitro statin concentrations often exceed what oral dosing achieves in tumor tissue
The tumor-suppressive benefit assumes gain-of-function activity from mutant p53 in this tumor, which has not been shown for this patient's biology
Retrospective statin-and-cancer epidemiology is confounded and should not be read as support
caveats: A decade-old finding with limited independent replication in pancreatic models, and no in-vivo Y220C-specific experiment.

intervention_label: [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-zolbetuximab (CLDN18.2 antibody radioconjugate)
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: A CLDN18.2 antibody carries lutetium-177 to the tumor, and the beta emission deposits dose over a path of roughly a millimetre. Killing therefore does not require every cell to carry the antigen: cells within crossfire range of a bound antibody take the dose too. The paired 89Zr imaging agent measures target engagement before treatment rather than inferring it from an archival stain.
rationale: At 2+/3+ in 60% of cells this tumor has a real but patchy antigen, and 40% of cells would be invisible to a naked antibody or a non-bystander payload. Crossfire is the one mechanism that turns heterogeneity from a liability into something tolerable. The MGH group showed tumor-selective uptake and, at 14.8 MBq, complete regression of most HUPT-4 PDAC xenografts with improved 90-day survival and a clean 90-day toxicity read.
novelty: This specific radioconjugate has no registered trial and sits at proof-of-concept in mice; no radioligand of any kind appears in this case's trials or clinical-evidence files.

key_manuscripts.finding: [89Zr]Zr-DFO-zolbetuximab showed high, IgG-controlled tumor uptake in gastric and PDAC xenografts, and a single 14.8 MBq dose of [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-zolbetuximab shrank GSU and PATU8988S tumors and drove complete regression of most HUPT-4 PDAC tumors with better 90-day survival. Toxicity assessment over 90 days was favorable.

model_systems: bulk and single-cell RNA-seq from 31 PDAC patients
developability: Built from an approved antibody and a widely used radionuclide with established chelation and dosimetry, so the translational path is unusually short by horizon-scan standards. A first-in-human study would need GMP radiolabelling, dosimetry, and marrow and renal safety work.
risks: CLDN18.2 is expressed on normal gastric mucosa, and a radioconjugate deposits dose there as well; gastric and marrow toxicity in humans is unmeasured
Subcutaneous xenografts have none of the desmoplastic barrier that limits antibody delivery in real PDAC, so uptake in this patient's tumor would likely be lower
The 60% antigen fraction in this case is below what the xenograft lines express; crossfire helps but does not make antigen density irrelevant
Access to lutetium-177 production and radiopharmacy limits where this could ever be done
caveats: One publication from one group. A different CLDN18.2 radioligand (177Lu-DOTA-SNA040) has just opened a first-in-human study, so this class is crossing into the clinical track and may not stay a horizon item for long.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 CAR-T armored with secreted hyaluronidase (sPH20-IgG2)
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: Hyaluronan-rich matrix physically restricts T-cell mobility in PDAC, so transferred cells stall before reaching antigen. Engineering the CAR construct to secrete PH20 hyaluronidase puts the enzyme where the cells are, continuously, instead of relying on a systemic dose that failed to help in HALO-301. The armoring is a delivery fix and leaves the CLDN18.2 recognition domain untouched.
rationale: The standing explanation for why CLDN18.2 cell therapy reads better in gastric cancer than in PDAC is the stroma, not the antigen, and satri-cel data in this case's files are dominated by gastric experience. Zhao's group showed hyaluronan restricted CAR-T migration, that sPH20-IgG2 secretion restored transmigration without blunting cytotoxicity, and that armored cells produced smaller tumors in vivo. Applying the same armoring to a CLDN18.2 binder is a construct-level change, not a new target.
novelty: No CLDN18.2 CAR carrying a stroma-degrading enzyme is in trials; the armored construct upstream (AZD6422) carries a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor, which addresses suppression rather than physical exclusion.

key_manuscripts.finding: Hyaluronan blocked anti-mesothelin CAR-T mobility in vitro, and a secreted PH20-IgG2 module restored transmigration through HA matrix without changing cytotoxicity or cytokine release. Armored cells infiltrated BGC823 and MKN28 xenografts better and produced smaller tumors than unarmored CAR-T.
Co-expressing IL-7 and PH20 in anti-GPC3 CAR-T improved tumor suppression in vitro and in vivo, a second antigen showing that the enzyme-armoring approach travels across constructs.

developability: Constructing it is routine cell-engineering work, but it means a new IND-stage product rather than a modification of an existing one, and CAR manufacturing for a patient with progressive disease is a timing problem in itself.
risks: Every supporting experiment used a different antigen (mesothelin, GPC3) in non-pancreatic models; no CLDN18.2 version has been built
On-target gastric mucosal toxicity of CLDN18.2 CAR-T is construct-independent, and better tumor penetration does nothing to reduce it
Systemic hyaluronidase caused thromboembolic events in the PEGPH20 program; local secretion should lower but not remove that concern
Degrading matrix could ease tumor-cell dissemination as well as T-cell entry
caveats: Class-level inference from other antigens; treat the CLDN18.2 version as untested.

intervention_label: Pharmacologic induction of CLDN18.2 (hypomethylating agent as antigen-density priming)
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: CLDN18.2 transcription in pancreatic cells runs through PKC and MAPK signaling onto an AP-1 site, and a CpG island in the CLDN18 coding sequence gates how much of that signal gets through. Demethylation lifts the gate. Raising antigen on the 40% of cells that currently stain negative would matter more for a threshold-gated therapy than any change in the cells that already stain 3+.
rationale: The single weakest point in this patient's strongest handle is that 60% of cells carry the antigen and 40% do not, which is what puts the tumor below the zolbetuximab registrational cutoff. Ito's group showed 5-aza-deoxycytidine amplified CLDN18a2 induction in two PDAC lines, HPAF-II and HPAC. A priming strategy that raised expression before a CLDN18.2 antibody, ADC, or cell product would target the eligibility problem rather than working around it; hypomethylation would also raise antigen presentation broadly, which is not irrelevant in a tumor with TMB 0.83.
novelty: No program or trial uses a hypomethylating agent to raise CLDN18.2 before a CLDN18.2-directed therapy in any tumor type; nothing on antigen induction appears upstream.

key_manuscripts.finding: CLDN18a2 mRNA was strongly induced by PKC activation in four pancreatic cancer lines, and a CpG island within the CLDN18 coding sequence was identified; 5-aza-deoxycytidine enhanced that induction in HPAF-II and HPAC but not in normal-derived hTERT-HPDE cells.

model_systems: HPAF-II, HPAC, PANC-1, BxPC-3 pancreatic lines
developability: Decitabine and azacitidine are approved and cheap, so a short priming schedule before a CLDN18.2 agent is easy to write. What is missing is any demonstration that a tolerable human dose moves CLDN18.2 protein at the membrane, which is the only thing an IHC cutoff or a CAR cares about.
risks: The effect was seen as an amplifier of phorbol-ester-driven induction, not as standalone demethylation, so the standalone effect may be small or absent
Raising CLDN18.2 on normal gastric mucosa would widen the on-target toxicity margin problem for any CLDN18.2 therapy
Hypomethylating agents cause myelosuppression, which is a real cost in a patient heading toward cell therapy or further chemotherapy
Fifteen-year-old cell-line data with no in-vivo or patient-tissue confirmation
caveats: Mechanistically plausible and practically cheap to test, but the evidence is one old in-vitro paper.

intervention_label: Purine-synthesis blockade in COMPASS-mutant cells (lometrexol / GARFT inhibition)
mechanism: Losing MLL3/MLL4 enhancer function shifts metabolism toward de novo purine synthesis, with MLL1/COMPASS compensation underlying the shift. That leaves the cell leaning on a pathway the intact cell does not need as badly. Lometrexol inhibits GAR formyltransferase in that pathway, so the dependency becomes a drug target.
rationale: KMT2C S2816fs is the feature with the thinnest actionability in this case, and the honest answer so far has been that nothing translatable exists. Shilatifard's group ran CRISPR dropout screens in MLL3/4-depleted cells, found synthetic lethality on purine and pyrimidine synthesis, and showed MLL3/MLL4-mutant tumors were sensitive to lometrexol in culture and in animals. That is a specific, testable dependency rather than a general epigenetic-agent hypothesis.
novelty: Lometrexol has no active oncology program and no trial selects patients by KMT2C or KMT2D mutation; nothing in this case's upstream files touches purine metabolism.

key_manuscripts.finding: CRISPR dropout screens in MLL3/4-depleted mouse ES cells showed synthetic lethality on purine and pyrimidine synthesis, metabolic and proteomic profiling confirmed increased purine synthesis, and MLL3/4-mutant tumors were sensitive to lometrexol in vitro and in vivo.

model_systems: mouse tumor models with MLL3/4 mutation
developability: Lometrexol was dosed in humans decades ago and shelved for toxicity, so the pharmacology exists but the sponsor does not. A modern attempt would more likely use an antifolate already in use, or a newer purine-pathway agent, with folate supplementation to manage the toxicity that stopped the original program.
risks: Lometrexol's clinical history is one of severe, unpredictable myelosuppression and mucositis, which is why it was abandoned
The supporting biology is a double MLL3/MLL4 knockout in mouse ES cells; this patient has a single-allele KMT2C frameshift in a human tumor, and the dependency may not be as deep
No pancreatic model anywhere in the supporting work
Whether S2816fs actually abolishes the relevant enhancer function has not been shown for this variant
caveats: The gap between a mouse ES-cell double knockout and a PDAC with one KMT2C frameshift is the main thing that would have to be closed before this means anything.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition gated on KMT2C loss rather than BRCA status
mechanism: KMT2C has a role at DNA damage sites that has nothing to do with promoter transcription: it is recruited by Ago2 and damage-response RNAs, methylates H3K4 locally, relaxes chromatin, and lets repair factors assemble. Losing it degrades homologous recombination, which is the same functional state that makes BRCA-mutant tumors sensitive to PARP inhibitors. The gate here is a chromatin gene rather than a canonical HR gene.
rationale: Chang and colleagues showed KMT2C/D mutations sensitized NSCLC models to PARP inhibitors and argued for those mutations as a biomarker in tumors where BRCA1/2 mutations are rare. This patient carries a KMT2C frameshift, has had 10 cycles of platinum-containing therapy, and the germline panel is still pending, so if the germline comes back negative this is the only remaining argument for a PARP inhibitor in this case. It is a hypothesis about biomarker scope, not about a new drug.
novelty: No trial selects patients for PARP inhibition by KMT2C status, and the olaparib rows upstream are strictly germline-BRCA maintenance, a different population and a different rationale.

key_manuscripts.finding: KMT2C was recruited to DNA damage sites by Ago2 and damage-response RNAs and amplified DDR signaling along chromatin; KMT2C/D mutations disrupted homologous recombination and sensitized NSCLC models to PARP inhibitors, which the authors proposed as a biomarker where BRCA1/2 mutation rates are low.

model_systems: NSCLC cell lines and xenografts with KMT2C/D mutation
developability: The drugs are approved and available, so this is a biomarker-qualification question. The step that matters is a functional HRD readout on this patient's tumor, since a frameshift call alone does not prove the repair defect is present.
risks: A single laboratory's result in NSCLC; independent replication in other tumor types is thin
KMT2C S2816fs is heterozygous on the report and may leave enough function that HR stays intact
Platinum exposure across 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles without durable control argues against a deep HR defect in this tumor
Functional HRD assays for PDAC are not standardised, so the gating test does not really exist yet
caveats: The claim is about which biomarker opens the PARP door, not about a new agent, and it should not be read as support for using a PARP inhibitor in this patient today.

intervention_label: Targeting the neural-like progenitor regeneration state that survives chemotherapy (GLIS3, IL-1beta axis)
target_feature_label: Clinical course: node-negative R0 resection with early recurrence
mechanism: Residual PDAC after neoadjuvant treatment is enriched for a neural-like progenitor transcriptional program, and recent work reframes that program as the normal pancreatic injury-regeneration response co-opted by tumor cells recovering from cytotoxic damage. GLIS3 came out as the transcription factor that drives clonogenicity, growth, and metastasis in that state, with IL-1beta inflammatory signaling implicated as a microenvironmental driver. Suppressing the state, rather than the bulk tumor, is the idea.
rationale: This patient had a good pathological response, 0/34 nodes, TRG 2, and still recurred four months after adjuvant therapy ended, which is the clinical shape of residual disease in a persistent state rather than of bulk chemoresistance. The regeneration-program framing gives that observation a mechanism and a handle. Nothing here is a drug yet, which is why it sits in this file rather than anywhere else.
novelty: No agent targets this program and no trial selects for it; upstream coverage of the neural-like progenitor state is descriptive spatial-transcriptomics work with no intervention attached.

key_manuscripts.finding: The neural-like progenitor signature enriched in post-treatment residual PDAC matched normal pancreatic injury and regeneration programs, and isogenic mouse organoid overexpression identified Glis3 as a driver of clonogenicity, tumor growth, and metastasis. IL-1beta-associated inflammatory signaling was implicated as a microenvironmental driver.

model_systems: isogenic mouse PDAC organoid transcription-factor overexpression
developability: GLIS3 is an undrugged transcription factor and there is no tool compound. The nearest tractable edge is the IL-1beta arm, where clinical-grade blockade exists, but that association is correlative in this paper and IL-1 blockade in PDAC has already disappointed.
risks: No compound, no target validation, and a transcription factor as the nominated node
A regeneration program shared with normal pancreatic injury repair is a poor candidate for a wide therapeutic window
The IL-1beta link is associative, and the causal experiments have not been done
This patient's recurrence has not been biopsied, so whether the state is present is unknown and currently unknowable
caveats: Included to keep the early-recurrence feature from silently dropping out of the horizon scan; it is a research question, not a candidate therapy.

intervention_label: alpha,beta-diketoamide covalent ligands of K-Ras(G12R)
mechanism: Arginine-reactive diketoamide electrophiles bind the switch II pocket and condense irreversibly with the guanidinium nitrogens of arginine 12, giving mutant selectivity without a cysteine.
rationale: The only G12R-selective chemistry in the literature and the obvious first stop for this feature, but the researcher already logged it, and four years on it still has no cellular potency, no pathway data, and no animal work.
exclusion_reason: Already surfaced upstream in preclinical_evidence.jsonl as the G12R covalent-chemistry row; logging it again would duplicate the researcher's coverage rather than extend it.

intervention_label: ERK/MEK inhibition combined with autophagy blockade
mechanism: Suppressing MAPK output triggers LKB1-AMPK-ULK1-driven autophagy, which buffers the loss; adding chloroquine or an ULK1 inhibitor removes the buffer.
rationale: An allele-linked vulnerability with real PDAC in-vivo support, and a plausible fit for a tumor whose driver produces lower ERK output to begin with.
exclusion_reason: Already carried upstream in preclinical_evidence.jsonl as an allele-linked vulnerability row, so it is the researcher's, not a new horizon candidate.

intervention_label: AKT inhibition to block the G12R dedifferentiation program
mechanism: G12R depends on AKT signaling to license acinar-to-ductal lineage reversion and the enhancer reprogramming that goes with it, so AKT blockade would in principle hold the differentiation state.
rationale: A genuinely allele-specific piece of biology and one of the more interesting recent G12R findings.
exclusion_reason: AKT inhibitors are clinical-stage with existing PDAC trial history, so a candidate built on them belongs to trial_screener rather than to a pre-clinical horizon scan.

intervention_label: CDK4/6 inhibition combined with KRAS pathway inhibition
mechanism: Simultaneous KRAS and CDK4 blockade produces durable growth arrest in PDAC cells that neither agent achieves alone.
rationale: Recent preclinical work supports the pairing in pancreatic models.
exclusion_reason: Both halves are clinical-stage and CDK4/6-plus-targeted-agent combinations are already in trials in solid tumors, so this sits above the development ceiling for this file.

intervention_label: KPT-9274 (PAK4/NAMPT dual inhibitor) with a KRAS inhibitor
mechanism: PAK4 and NAMPT blockade potentiates KRAS inhibitor activity in pancreatic and lung models.
rationale: Surfaced while scanning for KRAS-inhibitor potentiators with PDAC in-vivo data.
exclusion_reason: KPT-9274 has already been dosed in humans in phase 1 solid-tumor and haematologic studies, which puts it in trial_screener's territory.

intervention_label: Stromal normalization agents (losartan, minnelide) for PDAC drug delivery
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: Lowering CAF-driven collagen and hyaluronan production reduces interstitial pressure and re-expands collapsed vessels, improving perfusion and macromolecule delivery.
rationale: The current preclinical answer to the delivery problem that sank PEGPH20, and delivery is the standing explanation for why antibody and cell therapies underperform in PDAC relative to gastric cancer.
exclusion_reason: Both agents have been through PDAC clinical trials, and neither acts on a stated targetable feature; the stromal barrier is context for this case rather than a listed target.

intervention_label: AZD6422 (TGF-beta-armored CLDN18.2 CAR-T)
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: A CD28/CD3-zeta CLDN18.2 CAR carrying a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor so stromal TGF-beta cannot suppress the transferred cells.
rationale: The closest published relative of the enzyme-armored construct kept above, and a direct answer to the suppressive PDAC microenvironment.
exclusion_reason: Already logged upstream in preclinical_evidence.jsonl as the armored-CAR class mechanism, so it is covered rather than novel here.

intervention_label: Ferroptosis induction in KMT2C-deficient cells
mechanism: KMT2C loss has been linked to a shift in lipid-peroxidation handling that leaves cells more sensitive to ferroptotic death.
rationale: One of the few published KMT2C-loss vulnerabilities, and worth checking given how little else exists for this feature.
exclusion_reason: Already surfaced upstream in preclinical_evidence.jsonl from the meningioma work, and the tumor context is too distant to build a separate candidate on.

intervention_label: 177Lu-DOTA-SNA040 (CLDN18.2 peptide radioligand) with 68Ga companion imaging
target_feature_label: CLDN18.2 expression, 2+/3+ in 60% of tumor cells
mechanism: A CLDN18.2-binding peptide labelled with lutetium-177, with a gallium-68 imaging analogue used to screen out patients whose tumors show no uptake.
rationale: Found while checking whether the CLDN18.2 radioligand class had crossed into humans; it enrolls pancreatic cancer among its solid-tumor cohorts.
exclusion_reason: Recruiting in a first-in-human dose-escalation study (NCT07595237), so it is clinical-stage and belongs to trial_screener; noted here because that screen did not surface it and the case team may want it.
